---
title: "Figure conventions and reproducibility"
---

Walkthrough figures are drawn with **R and ggplot2**, from one shared theme in
`figures/style.R` and the figure jobs in `figures/render.R`. The walkthroughs
compute with Python and pass the points to R for drawing. Benchmark and
verification charts are drawn by phpstats.org from the evidence records. The
extension itself has no graphics or R dependency.

## Visual conventions

- Conceptual figures use blue for the reference/population curve, green for the
  conditional/native curve, orange for an approximation or boundary, and gray for
  observations. Their legends describe the statistical quantity rather than imply
  that a curve is an implementation comparison.
- Use a white background, common sans-serif type, restrained grids and explicit
  quantity/unit labels. Titles state what is shown; captions state the data or
  approximation, transformations and relevant limits.
- Bar charts start at zero. Log scales are explicit and reserved for quantities
  spanning orders of magnitude.

Each figure is saved as an **SVG** with selectable text and a **160-dpi PNG**,
at fixed dimensions recorded in the [figure manifest](figures/manifest.json). The
font family is generic sans-serif, so the resolved font can differ across
platforms. The conventions use ggplot2's
[themes](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html) and
[export controls](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsave.html).

## Generate figures without running fits or benchmarks

Install the documentation-only R packages:

```r
install.packages(c("ggplot2", "jsonlite", "svglite"),
                 repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
```

From the repository root:

```sh
Rscript docs/figures/render.R --all
# Or one figure:
Rscript docs/figures/render.R profile
Rscript docs/figures/render.R posterior
./scripts/render-docs
```

- The renderer reads the points in `figures/data/`, which the executable
  walkthroughs export. It does not call estimators or regenerate fixtures.
  Re-executing those pages updates the point snapshots and figures.
- SVGs are embedded with namespaced clip IDs, so figures on one page do not
  interfere.
- An ordinary site render reuses frozen outputs and saved images. Re-executing
  the computational notebooks needs the [documentation environment](documentation.qmd).

The [manifest](figures/manifest.json) records each input's path and MD5, the image
hashes and dimensions, the renderer and theme hashes, the R version, the platform,
and the direct package versions. [The R package record](figures/r-packages.json)
adds the transitive dependency versions. Other versions may not reproduce the
figures byte for byte.

## Existing figure coverage

The renderer draws:

- `profile`: the Gaussian likelihood profile in the [random-intercept walkthrough](notebooks/lmm-math.qmd)
- `posterior`: the conditional random-intercept distribution in the
  [binomial walkthrough](notebooks/logistic-mixed-math.qmd)
